messages:
Alex: FYI seeing p99 jump on hosted-api in ap-south-1 around 1912345678, p99 ~760ms, p95 ~380ms
Observability-bot: alert: hosted-api.ap-south-1 p99_latency > 700ms (5m)
Maya: dashboards show allocator-dispatcher queue_depth rising sharply and token_waiters increasing; GPUs at 48% util.
Tomas: any config changes pushed today? rate-limiter hysteresis tweak merged last night?
Deploy-bot: rollout: runtime-2.0.1 (rate-limiter hysteresis + batching-snap) -> ap-south-1 @1912345600 by ci/cd
Sara: runtime-2.0.1 reduced batch_max_delay_ms from 20 -> 8 and changed rate-limiter hysteresis to be more aggressive for tenant bursts.
Alex: pulled a flame graph from the incident window. Hot stacks:
```
32% dispatcher::route_batch_to_allocator()
26% kernel_selector::evaluate_candidates()
15% batcher::waiting_for_tokens()
11% kv_cache::evict_hot_prefix()
```
Maya: kv cache hit rate dropped 94%->69% during the window; eviction spikes line up with tenant churn.
Tomas: the dispatcher is doing more frequent routing decisions because batches are smaller; that increases kernel switching overhead.
Alex: also seeing increased kernel_switch_count metric per-second, and many batches pick fallback_cpu_kernel for mixed-length batches.
Sara: hypothesis: aggressive hysteresis + lower batch_max_delay => tiny batches; combined with tenant mixing (T-77 doing interleaved long reads), we get kernel thrash and eviction storms.
Maya: tenant T-77 shows lots of alternating short Q&A requests and long-document summarizations, seq variance per-window ~0.7.
Alex: snippet from runtime config in v2.0.1:
```
if (batch_delay_ms <= 8) prefer(LOW_LATENCY_KERNEL);
if (seq_variance > 0.5) force(FALLBACK_CPU_KERNEL);
```
Tomas: that seq_variance threshold looks lower than before. Also dispatcher now evicts prefixed cache entries more eagerly under memory pressure.
Sara: immediate mitigations proposed: 1) revert batch_max_delay_ms to 20ms on a canary subset 2) increase kv_cache.shard_headroom +25% on hot allocators 3) enable debug logging for dispatcher routing decisions.
Alex: I'll craft a canary revert for runtime-2.0.2 that restores batch_max_delay_ms and relaxes seq_variance threshold.
Deploy-bot: canary deploy: runtime-2.0.2-canary -> allocator-dispatcher-A1 @1912345710
Maya: after canary: canary p95 -> 130ms, p99 -> 210ms for that subset; overall cluster still p99 ~480ms. kv cache bump applied to A1 and A2.
Observability-bot: config change: kv_cache.shard_headroom +25% applied to allocator-dispatcher-A1/A2 @1912345730
Sara: good signal that heuristics change is main factor. Next steps: full rollback if canary holds 15m, but we should also add instrumentation to correlate kernel_switch_count with per-tenant seq variance and cache eviction buckets.
Tomas: agree. Longer-term: add dispatcher-level adaptive batching: detect high seq_variance in a short window and route those requests to a separate pooling path that prefers throughput-friendly kernels, rather than forcing fallback CPU kernels.
Alex: created PERF-1202 with flamegraphs, kernel_switch histograms, and tenant fingerprints (T-77 highlighted).
Maya: added temporary trace: log dispatcher decisions when batch_size < 4 or seq_variance > 0.4 for 20m.
Sara: also decision: pause any further runtime-2.x heuristic rollouts until we have an automated mixed-sequence ST (synthetic test) and metric guard for kernel_switch_rate.
Alex: running synthetic workload now: mix 12% long-context (8k tokens) + 88% short (64 tokens) across 20 tenants to validate adaptive path.
Tomas: I'll sketch a PR for adaptive dispatcher + an e2e test to reproduce eviction storms; aim to land in staging next week.
Maya: follow-up: if canary remains stable, do full rollback to 2.0.2 by 1912345970; keep kv_cache headroom bump until eviction root cause identified.
Alex: someone please ping infra on-call to prepare a manual kv_cache rollback plan if memory pressure rises after headroom changes.
Sara: noted. Thanks team 44d Keeping this thread for the triage timeline and action items.
Maya: uploading dashboard snapshots and the synthetic run plan to PERF-1202.
Tomas: will run extra perf sweeps on kernel candidate penalties tomorrow UTC.
Alex: if we see another spike, @here escalate to eng-runtime pager (incidents channel).
